stages.name: Non-price competition
stages.title: Non-price competition
stages.sub: Recognise the different ways firms compete for customers without cutting price.

steps.q: Two petrol stations sell identical fuel side by side. If one station wants more customers without changing the fuel itself, could cutting its price below the rival's win buyers?
steps.right: Yes, a lower price alone can win buyers
steps.wrong: No, a lower price changes nothing
steps.hint: The fuel is identical, so what is the only thing left for a driver to compare?

steps.q: Coffee-chain A keeps its price the same as its rival but runs campaigns showing why its coffee tastes better. Is this competing on price?
steps.right: No, it is trying to change what people think
steps.wrong: Yes, it is really a hidden discount
steps.hint: Has the price tag changed at all?

steps.q: Two colas taste almost the same in blind tests, yet many people insist on the one with the familiar red logo. Are they reacting to the price or to something else?
steps.right: Something else, the image built around it
steps.wrong: The price, since it seems cheaper
steps.hint: The taste test showed the drinks are nearly identical, so what is driving the preference?

steps.q: A supermarket gives you points on every purchase that turn into vouchers, encouraging you to keep shopping there rather than a rival at the same prices. Does this change the shelf price you see today?
steps.right: No, it rewards repeat buying instead
steps.hint: Look at the price on the shelf itself: has it moved?

steps.prompt: Drag and drop the 4 key terms in the order they build on each other.

steps.q: Two phone brands cost the same, but one offers a longer warranty and better build quality. If a buyer picks that one, are they responding to a lower price?
steps.right: No, they are responding to the build and support
steps.wrong: Yes, warranties always mean a lower price
steps.hint: The price tag is identical between the two phones, so what is swaying the buyer?

steps.q: An oligopoly firm uses adverts, branding, loyalty points and better after-sales service all at once, but never changes its price. What overall name covers this whole group of tactics?
steps.right: Ways of competing that do not involve price
steps.wrong: A form of price competition in disguise
steps.hint: None of these tactics touch the price tag, so what do they have in common?
